title: Add a user to Experience Platform
t1: Add the user's email address to the default AEP product profile in Adobe Admin Console so that the user exists in the system.
t2: In the Experience Platform UI, navigate to Permissions, go to Roles, and create a new role by selecting desired sandbox access and feature permission categories.
t3: Add the user to the newly created role so they are granted access to the configured Experience Platform features and sandboxes.

title: Set up a data source and build real-time customer profiles
source: Behind the scenes: A customer experience powered by Experience Platform
t1: Define a schema using Experience Data Model (XDM) to express the structure of your data source, including which fields represent customer identities.
t2: Create a dataset and begin ingesting data into Experience Platform, either via streaming or batch ingestion, using the defined schema.
t3: Experience Platform builds a real-time customer profile for each customer by merging incoming data fragments using the identity graph.

title: Build and activate a segment-based email campaign
t1: Ingest customer data from multiple sources and normalize it by mapping each source to standardized XDM schemas.
t2: Use the Segment Builder in Experience Platform to create an audience based on customer attributes and behavioral events.
t3: Activate the audience to an email marketing destination to deliver a targeted campaign to qualifying customer profiles.

title: Run an AI-powered customer churn prevention campaign
t1: Use Customer AI to train a machine learning model that predicts each customer's likelihood to churn, generating propensity scores.
t2: Create an audience segment that filters customer profiles with high churn propensity scores using the Segment Builder.
t3: Activate the high-risk audience across email and other channels with personalized win-back offers using Journey Optimizer.

title: Re-engage customers who abandoned their cart
t1: Run real-time journey analysis in Experience Platform to identify customers who added items to a cart but did not complete checkout.
t2: Create a re-engagement segment based on the cart abandonment event, filtering by customer consent preferences.
t3: Activate the segment in Journey Optimizer to send personalized re-engagement messages across email, push, and other channels.

title: Ingest streaming data and update the identity graph
t1: Send customer interaction events to Experience Platform in real time using the Web SDK or a streaming API endpoint.
t2: Experience Platform stores the incoming data in the data lake and flags it for immediate processing into the real-time customer profile.
t3: The identity graph links the new data fragment to the customer's existing identities, updating their unified profile in real time.

title: Resolve an anonymous visitor's identity on login
t1: An anonymous customer visits the website from a new device and a device ID is captured as their only initial identity.
t2: The customer logs in and Identity Service detects the link between the device ID and their known identifiers such as CRM ID and email address.
t3: Experience Platform merges the anonymous device fragment into the customer's existing unified profile using the updated identity graph.

title: Set up data governance labels and policies
t1: A data steward applies usage labels to individual data fields in Experience Platform to mark them according to their sensitivity or contractual restrictions.
t2: The data steward creates a data usage policy that blocks labeled fields from being sent to specific destination types, such as third-party ad networks.
t3: Experience Platform automatically enforces the policy and prevents activation when a marketer tries to send restricted data to a blocked destination.

title: Plan and implement an Experience Platform project
t1: During the planning phase, the enterprise architect meets with stakeholders to document business objectives and produce an implementation architecture.
t2: During the implementation phase, data architects model incoming data into XDM schemas and data engineers create datasets and ingest data into Platform.
t3: During the use phase, marketers configure platform services such as Real-Time CDP and Journey Optimizer to deliver business value against the original objectives.

title: Personalize a returning customer's web experience
t1: A known customer makes a purchase while logged in, and the event is captured and stored in their real-time customer profile in Experience Platform.
t2: The customer returns to the site without logging in, and the identity graph links their anonymous device ID to their known profile using contextual identifiers.
t3: Experience Platform uses the customer's unified behavioral history to deliver a personalized on-site experience even though the customer is not authenticated.
